newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers continue to slip on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers continue to slip on Iraq.

text.p: North American bunker prices continued to slip this week, finding weakness in final U.N. approval for the sale of Iraqi oil on the world market, players said on Tuesday.

Trade was active in the East Coast, as many players tried to sell off barrels in anticipation the market may come down further. The market is also feeling some of the bearishness of warm weather forecasts for the region.
"We could go farther down if the panic continues," said one East Coast trader.
Prices of New York 380 CST fell $6 a tonne to between $120 a tonne and $122 a tonne, with 180 CST offered at $124, about $8 below levels last Thursday.
On the West Coast, Seattle 380 CST slipped $1 to $128/129, while 180 CST dropped $4 to $130/131, traders said.
"The Iraqi news has affected us in that the market is long on fuel and short on demand. The numbers are slipping off," said a West Coast trader.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631
